API reference

Web layer

Web layer: the Flask application factory and its routes.

The factory takes the scraper, the loader, the analysis provider and the job runner as arguments, so the test suite can inject fakes and never touch the network. Pipeline state is held in a single PullState object that the tests can read and write directly – busy-state behaviour is therefore observable and injectable rather than timing dependent.

Routes

GET /

Redirect to /analysis.

GET /analysis

The analysis page: both buttons plus one Answer: per question.

POST /pull-data

Scrape and load new rows. 200 {"ok": true} when it ran, 202 when handed to a background runner, 409 {"busy": true} when a pull is already in progress, 500 {"ok": false} when the loader failed.

POST /update-analysis

Recompute the analysis. 200 {"ok": true}, or 409 {"busy": true} while a pull is in progress (in which case nothing is recomputed).

GET /status

JSON snapshot of PullState, used by the page and by tests.

src.flask_app.create_app(config=None, scraper=None, loader=None, analysis_provider=None, rows_provider=None, runner=None, state=None)[source]

Build and return a configured Flask application.

Parameters:

  • config (Dict[str, Any] | None) – values merged into app.config; DATABASE_URL is honoured by the default loader/analysis providers.

  • scraper (Callable[[], List[Dict[str, Any]]] | None) – callable returning a list of raw records. Defaults to src.scrape.pull_new_records().

  • loader (Callable[[List[Dict[str, Any]]], int] | None) – callable taking those records and returning the number of new rows. Defaults to src.load_data.insert_rows().

  • analysis_provider (Callable[[], Dict[str, Any]] | None) – callable returning the analysis dict. Defaults to src.query_data.get_analysis().

  • rows_provider (Callable[[], List[Dict[str, Any]]] | None) – callable returning recent rows for the page table. Defaults to src.query_data.get_recent_rows().

  • runner (Callable[[Callable[[], None]], Any] | None) – callable that executes the pull job. Defaults to run_sync(); pass run_in_thread() for background pulls.

  • state (PullState | None) – pre-built PullState, handy for seeding a busy state.

Returns:

the application, with the service bundle in app.extensions["gradcafe"].

Return type:

Flask

ETL: extract

ETL extract layer: pull applicant entries from The Grad Café.

The scraper separates fetching a page from parsing it. Fetching goes through an injectable page_source_provider callable, which defaults to a Selenium-driven Chrome session; the test suite passes a provider that returns canned HTML, so no test ever touches the network.

ETL: transform

ETL transform layer: sanitise raw scraped records.

clean_records() is deliberately conservative – it normalises whitespace and coerces the numeric fields, but leaves the record keys exactly as the scraper produced them so that src.load_data.normalize_record() remains the single place where database columns are decided.

ETL: load

ETL load layer: normalise Grad Café records and write them to PostgreSQL.

The module owns three responsibilities:

  1. the applicants table definition (CREATE_TABLE_SQL),

  2. turning a raw scraped/cleaned record into a database row (normalize_record()),

  3. an idempotent bulk insert (insert_rows()).

Uniqueness policy

p_id is the primary key and is derived from the record rather than assigned by the database: the numeric id inside the Grad Café result URL when one is present, otherwise a deterministic hash of the record’s identifying fields (see derive_p_id()). Inserts use ON CONFLICT (p_id) DO NOTHING, so re-pulling data that is already stored is a no-op.

src.load_data.REQUIRED_FIELDS: Sequence[str] = ('p_id', 'program', 'comments', 'url', 'status', 'term', 'us_or_international', 'degree')

Columns that may never be NULL; normalize_record() always fills them.

src.load_data.COLUMNS: Sequence[str] = ('p_id', 'program', 'comments', 'date_added', 'url', 'status', 'term', 'us_or_international', 'gpa', 'gre', 'gre_v', 'gre_aw', 'degree', 'llm_generated_program', 'llm_generated_university')

Every column of the applicants table, in insert order.

src.load_data.derive_p_id(record, fallback=0)[source]

Derive the primary key for a record.

The Grad Café result URL (.../result/1020482) carries a stable numeric id, which makes re-pulled records collapse onto the same row. When no URL is available a deterministic hash of the identifying fields is used so that the same record still maps to the same p_id on every pull.

Parameters:

  • record (Dict[str, Any]) – raw or normalised record.

  • fallback (int) – value returned when the record carries no identity at all.

Return type:

int

src.load_data.normalize_record(record, index=1)[source]

Turn one raw record into a fully populated applicants row.

Accepts both the scraper’s raw key names ("GPA", "US/International", "llm-generated-program") and the database column names, so cleaned data and re-read database rows both normalise cleanly. Every column listed in REQUIRED_FIELDS is guaranteed to be non-NULL on the way out.

Parameters:

  • record (Dict[str, Any]) – the raw record.

  • index (int) – 1-based position in the batch, used only as a last-resort id.

Returns:

a dict keyed by COLUMNS.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

src.load_data.insert_rows(records, conn=None, database_url=None, normalize=True)[source]

Insert records into applicants and return how many rows were new.

The insert is idempotent: rows whose p_id already exists are skipped by ON CONFLICT (p_id) DO NOTHING, so the returned count is the number of genuinely new rows rather than the number of records supplied.

Parameters:

  • records (Iterable[Dict[str, Any]]) – raw records (normalize=True) or ready-made rows.

  • conn (Connection | None) – an existing connection to reuse; when None a new one is opened from DATABASE_URL and closed again before returning.

  • database_url (str | None) – connection-string override used when conn is None.

  • normalize (bool) – run normalize_record() over each record first.

Returns:

number of rows inserted.

Raises:

psycopg.Error – the whole batch is rolled back on any failure.

Return type:

int

Reporting

Reporting layer: the SQL behind the analysis page.

Each question rendered on /analysis is declared once as an AnalysisSpec – key, human question, formatting kind and SQL. That single declaration drives the raw values (get_analysis()), the formatted answers (get_analysis_items()) and the command-line report (run_queries()), so the page and the CLI can never drift apart.

Connections

Database connection helpers.

Every module reads the connection string from the DATABASE_URL environment variable so that the application, the test suite and CI can each point at a different PostgreSQL instance without code changes.

src.db.DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://localhost/gradcafe'

Used when DATABASE_URL is not set in the environment.

src.db.get_database_url(database_url=None)[source]

Return the PostgreSQL connection string to use.

Parameters:

database_url (str | None) – explicit override; when None the DATABASE_URL environment variable is used, falling back to DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL.

Returns:

a libpq connection string.

Return type:

str

src.db.sqlalchemy_url(database_url=None)[source]

Return get_database_url() rewritten for the SQLAlchemy psycopg driver.

postgresql://host/db becomes postgresql+psycopg://host/db so that SQLAlchemy uses psycopg 3 rather than the (unavailable) psycopg2 default.

Parameters:

database_url (str | None)

Return type:

str

src.db.connect(database_url=None, **kwargs)[source]

Open a new psycopg connection.

Parameters:

  • database_url (str | None) – optional connection-string override.

  • kwargs (Any) – forwarded to psycopg.connect().

Return type:

Connection
